findings.title: Resolve contradiction on whether a 'current' category list exists during open questions
findings.body: The Business Rules (line 338) and the first sentence of this section state that 'Exactly one sweep category list is current at any time' and 'Exactly one recorded category list version is current.' However, the subsequent sentences state that 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list... cannot be marked current.' AC6 (line 456) repeats this constraint. This creates a direct contradiction: the spec mandates a current list at all times, but also mandates that no list can be marked current while the open questions are unresolved. Clarify whether the 'current' constraint is suspended until the open questions are resolved, or if a provisional current list is permitted.

findings.title: Use Case 1 steps omit recording of uncategorized findings
findings.body: Step 3 states that Ronda records whether each category produced findings or none. However, AC20 requires that 'Every finding published by a sweep pass appears in the per-category pass record, either against one or more swept categories or as uncategorized.' The use case steps should explicitly mention that findings fitting no swept category are recorded as uncategorized in the per-category pass record, to align with the acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Terminal miss record omits sweep-off control miss code
findings.body: The spec defines a recorded sweep-off control as a 'compared reviewer' (AC15(b), Business Rules). However, the 'Terminal miss record' section defines code values only for the sweep-enabled review (`sweep_enabled_miss`) and the external reviewer (`external_review_miss`), and states the head is terminally adjudicated 'only when both are present'. If a sweep-off control is recorded for the head and also missed the defect, the spec provides no code value to record its miss, and does not state whether its presence is required for terminal adjudication. Define how a sweep-off control's miss is recorded and whether it is required for terminal adjudication of the head.

findings.title: Terminal miss record omits sweep-off control miss
findings.body: The spec defines the sweep-off control as a compared reviewer (Business Rules, AC15(b)), and states that a head is terminally adjudicated when all compared reviewers report no findings but human adjudication records a defect. However, the 'Terminal miss record' section only defines code values for `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss`, and explicitly states the head is terminally adjudicated 'only when both are present'. It provides no mechanism to record a sweep-off control's miss, nor does it clarify whether the presence of a sweep-off control that missed the defect blocks terminal adjudication. Add a code value for the sweep-off control miss and update the terminal adjudication condition to require it when a control is recorded, or explicitly state that the control's miss is exempt from this record.

findings.title: AC15(d) mischaracterizes AC9's model identity requirement
findings.body: AC15(d) states that 'AC9's "same model" binds only the two precision arms to each other', using this to justify requiring the precision runs to match the recall runs' model identity. However, AC9 explicitly requires the precision runs to be on 'the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count (the sample count AC8 requires for the recall runs)'. While the parenthetical only explicitly ties the sample count to AC8, the clear intent is to tie all four parameters to AC8's recall runs. AC15(d)'s claim that AC9 only binds the precision arms is a misreading of AC9's intent. Clarify AC9 to explicitly state that the precision runs must use the same model as the recall runs (as required by AC8), and remove the contradictory justification in AC15(d).

findings.title: Real-PR recall claim requires impossible benchmark precision conditions
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Decision-gate consistency matrix (Claim admissibility) state that a comparative real-PR recall claim requires paired precision evidence 'on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count... as the heads the claim is made over'. A real-PR claim is made over real pull request heads, not a benchmark fixture, so requiring a 'fixture version' and 'sample count' to match the real-PR heads is logically incoherent and impossible to satisfy. The Business Rules section and Coverage Matrix (O11) correctly omit 'fixture version and sample count' for real-PR claims. Remove the benchmark-specific 'fixture version, and sample count' phrasing from AC15(d) and the matrix to align with the Business Rules and O11.

findings.title: Fix conflation of benchmark and real-PR precision requirements in AC15(d) and the decision-gate matrix
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Claim admissibility gate require a comparative real-PR recall claim to be backed by 'paired precision evidence AC9 defines on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count... as the heads the claim is made over'. This conflates benchmark concepts (fixture version, sample count) with real-PR concepts (heads the claim is made over). Real-PR heads do not have a 'fixture version' or 'sample count' in the benchmark sense, making this requirement untestable and nonsensical for real-PR claims. Clarify whether real-PR recall claims require the benchmark precision evidence to be valid for the same model, or if real-PR precision evidence is expected (which contradicts AC9's benchmark focus).
